o1.biggest_strength: Six primary texts that are genuinely different angles (transparency, taste, no added sugar, protein and texture, 4 pm, price) in a blunt, witty voice. The launch plan is two clean pairs, each changing only the primary text, with a budget and keep/cut rules that check out (₹10,500 per ad buys about 36 purchases at ₹290).
o1.biggest_mistake: It tells the owner to pause the ₹340 and ₹380 ads to fund the test, which is a bold call with no check on whether those ads feed other goals. It also holds back the live no-added-sugar and protein angles.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a short fallback in case review quotes are not allowed, and soften the pause call into a staged shift of budget.

o2.biggest_strength: Opens with a clear read of the past 90 days: the winner was fatigued, not beaten, and taste and texture reviews never ran. It also adds a backup plan in case review quotes are not allowed.
o2.biggest_mistake: Five of the six primary texts repeat "12 g protein. No added sugar" as a tail, so the angles blur together, which is the sameness the owner hates.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Let each primary text carry a single distinct hook, and drop the repeated protein and sugar tail from most of them.

reason: Output 1 gives six truly different angles in a sharper voice, and its two-pair launch plan makes each test readable. Output 2 has good analysis, but most of its copy ends on the same "12 g protein, no added sugar" tail.
